title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1968-10-13
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > Sonic Solutions > EAC > CoolEdit > CD

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1968 show featuring a smoking Dark Star, soaring Eleven, and standout New Potato.
ai_review.review: The digitized soundboard tape delivers pristine vintage clarity with only minor splice quirks, letting the band’s remarkable interplay shine.  Listeners rave about the fresh, restrained chops, blazing guitar from Jerry, tight rhythm section, and unforgettable jams on Dark Star, Eleven, The Other One and New Potato.  Overall it’s a high‑energy performance that stands out as one of the best recordings from this era.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews, almost all 5‑star with consistent praise for both musical performance and audio fidelity; only minor criticisms that do not detract from the overall excellence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, high‑bit digitized tape with vintage warmth; a few listeners note a possible splice before drums, but sound is otherwise clean and well balanced.

poor_songs: New Potato (average, ends abruptly into drums)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set tight and focused with strong songcraft; second set expands into expansive jams that transport listeners back to the Haight‑era psychedelic vibe.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Blazing guitar work, especially on Dark Star and Death Don't Have No Mercy; vocal praised as soulful and powerful.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass feeding off the group with solid, “feeding each other” interplay throughout, highlighted in Eleven.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers described as fabulous and perfectly in sync during Dark Star and Eleven, though a later drum segment was seen as less compelling.
